principle: The component owns the composition. Atlas editorial work chooses the two strongest activity-specific chapter angles, gives each a short editorial label, and adds one complementary field note from verified information. The slots are never predefined as route, price, timing, history or any other topic.

presentation.chapterNumbering: 01 and 02 are presentation-owned and derive from chapter order
presentation.layout: two chapters on the left, one secondary Field Card photo on the right, one fixed-position post-it note

chapters.selectionRule: Choose two distinct angles that deserve explanation for this specific activity. Give each chapter a concise label that names its actual subject, then lead with what is most useful, distinctive or consequential in the verified material.
chapters.antiPattern: Do not fill chapter one with route or chapter two with price by habit. If access is trivial, admission is free, or another subject matters more, choose different angles and labels.

note.selectionRule: Use one concise field note that complements rather than repeats the chapters. It may cover route, price, clothing, timing, etiquette, weather, safety, equipment or another useful detail.

shape.chapters: exactly two { label, title, body } objects

generationInput.subsequentSections: When fieldCardPrimaryStory is supplied, candidate.sections contains only later Field Card chapters.
